Summary: This legislation would make it unlawful to store, handle, use or possess a powered bicycle, powered mobility device, or a storage battery for such devices, unless such equipment meets the relevant standards for sale established by local law.  The bill would also establish civil penalties for those who violate such possession ban. Additionally, the bill would amend existing penalties for the sale of such products, such that an individual would be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year imprisonment, in addition to civil penalty of up to $1,000 for each violation. Finally, a person who assembles or sells second-use storage battery would be liable for a civil penalty of up to $1,000 and would be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by up to 1 year imprisonment.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York and the New York city fire code, in relation to penalties for the possession, sale, lease, or rental of unsafe powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, and storage batteries and the assembly or sale of second-use lithium-ion batteries

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subdivision f of section 20-610 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as amended by local law number 50 for the year 2024, is amended to read as follows:
f. A person who violates this section, or any rule promulgated thereunder, [is liable for a civil penalty as follows] shall:
1. For [the first] each violation of subdivision a, b or c of this section, be liable for a civil penalty of [zero] not more than one thousand dollars and be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment for not more than 1 year; and
2. [For each subsequent violation of subdivision a, b or c of this section issued on a different day within two years of the date of a first violation, a civil penalty of not more than two thousand dollars; and
3.] For each [subsequent] violation of subdivision e or h of this section [issued on a different day within two years of the date of a first violation], be liable for a civil penalty of not more than five hundred dollars.
§ 2. Section FC 309 of the New York city fire code is amended by adding a new section 309.5 to read as follows:
309.5. Prohibition on storing, handling, using and possessing certain powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, and related storage batteries.  It shall be unlawful to store, handle, use or possess a powered bicycle, powered mobility device, or a storage battery for a powered bicycle or powered mobility device, as such terms of defined in section 20-610 of this code, unless such equipment meets the relevant standards for sale established by section 20-610 of this code.
§ 3. Section FC 109 of the New York city fire code is amended by adding a new section 109.2.6 to read as follows:
109.2.5 Penalties for violations related to second-use batteries. Any person who violates FC 309.3.5 shall be liable for a civil penalty of not more than $1,000 for each violation issued for the same offense on a different day within 2 years. Such person shall also be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment for not more than 1 year.
§ 4.   This local law takes effect immediately.
